newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks expected to stay tethered to 20,000.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks expected to stay tethered to 20,000.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are likely to stay tethered to the 20,000 threshold on Thursday, as signs of further strength in the yen against the dollar should make investors cautious, brokers said.
On Wednesday, the Nikkei 225 closed up 80.61 points, or 0.40 percent, at 20,209.72. Its June futures gained 60 points to end at 20,240.

"External factors are mixed as Wall Street and Nikkei futures in Chicago ended higher overnight while the yen strengthened beyond 116, which could be a negative factor," said Ken Ishikida, general manager at Sanyo Securities.
"If the yen powers far beyond 115, which is the level where most exporters set their currency rates at, serious selling could emerge," Yorita added.
Late in the morning, the yen slipped briefly past 116 yen to 115.85, the lowest since January 13.
Brokers said news that former Nomura Securities Co Ltd executives were arrested on Wednesday soured the mood for brokerages 0#SEC.T, bringing the sector to the top of the retreating sector list.
Nomura was the most heavily traded issue with a turnover of 4.95 million shares. It fell 70 yen to 1,410.
"There are still concerns about how business suspensions, which are weighing down the shares, will effect the brokerage," a broker at a "Big Four" brokerage said.

Banks 0#BNK.T were also weak, particularly trust banks. Sumitomo Trust & Banking Co Ltd, which was suspended from trade on Wednesday on unclear information surrounding the issuance of preferred shares, slid to 1,060 yen by midday, after closing at 1,230 yen on Tuesday.
Brokers said there were still oversupply worries in the market although company officials said although fund-raising was being considered, specific details were undecided.
